pages.transcription:
Wyndham Hotel
42 West 58th Street
New York

25. 7. 40

Dear Hanna,
I am in despair that
apparently something went wrong with
Eva's affidavit. By the time you get
this letter I hope to have settled
everything and you will be informed
by cable, but although it does not
help anything I wish to explain
the matter.
Two days after our arrival
we went to see Stephen Wise, the
well-known liberal rabbi, and during
the twenty minutes he had time
for us I mentioned that I was
anxious to bring my niece over but
that so far I did not know who could
help me with the affidavit. He imme-
diately said he would send the affi-
davit either himself or through the

committee, took down all the parti-
culars, promised to cable it, and the
next day when he saw Stefan again
he said it had been sent off.
We felt quite sure that every-
thing was all-right, I was very glad to
have settled the most essential part
so that you could proceed with all
the formalities. We did not cable you
because we felt so sure that the
affidavit had been sent and then by
a kind of over-cautiousness, not to send
you too many cables in such a short
period. I can't tell you how sorry I
am that I did not cable you about
it because then you would have
informed us very soon that you had
not received the affidavit. Instead
we waited quietly, feeling sure that
you were getting things ready and
would then cable us your decision.
Only when your cable arrived telling
me to do like Mr. Kuhn about the

law told me she would love to take
Eva for a short time and that she would
certainly look after her wherever she
goes, my brother-in-law has so far not
repeated the offer and I believe that
Anita with her two children - the girl
is 7 or 8 - would be easier and more
pleasant for Eva and it would be
better. On the whole, when we are away
I would rely most on Rose who is now
taking the two boys of Carmel and
who would certainly go and see Eva
and see that everything is all-right
for her. I can also rely upon her that
she will think of Eva should she
hear of a family willing to take a
girl.
Now I have told you the whole
story, I cannot tell you how sorry I am
that I did not cable you right at the
beginning and that therefore we did
not notice earlier that something has
gone wrong. But I hope it will still be time.

started and Mr. Kuhn is already in va-

wrote him at once and then I tried to
get exact information from Stephen
Wise, only to hear that he was also
away for a few weeks and that his
secretary had gone away as well. I
wrote him at once and am now
expecting his answer to learn what
has gone wrong and where the mistake
has been made. Then I shall try to
put it right at once and this time I
shall cable when the affidavit goes
off.
As to settling Eva I wrote
you that Anita would take her for
the beginning, and that I am expecting
the address of a good and reasonable
boarding school. Stefan's brother and
my sister-in-law are still at the

As to our plans, we cabled
you that we had postponed departure
until the 9th August. We are staying
in New York in spite of the heat which
is rather bad but not yet so terrible
as we expected. It is now a bit quieter,
many people are leaving New York
now, and Stefan is able to work re-
gularly every day although he still
finds concentration difficult in view
of the world events. By the time you
get this letter we will probably
just have left for Brazil. We are
not too eager to leave - it seems so
far away - and we hope to be able
to come back here after the South
American tour.
As to to you, we hope that
you are all well and that you have sent
us a letter to New York. I am waiting
very impatiently to hear from you
about the whole family and Levinthals.
Kindest regards to all,
Lotte
